name: First Territorial Capitol of Kansas
scope: Standing original territorial capitol at Pawnee within Fort Riley, with its limestone elevations, four entrances and simple shake roof.
era: Restored standing exterior after the 1927–28 works, retaining the original limestone walls and mid-nineteenth-century massing.

originalReview.notes: The first illustration on printed page 68 of the 1896 edition identifies the Pawnee capitol and shows two storeys of limestone, central doors, a simple gable and the rhythm of rectangular openings.

review.method: Exactly matched public-domain originals, native building footprint and published architectural dimensions.
review.notes: Checked the published Qualla story first. Its building photograph had inconsistent photographer affiliation in the source records, so it was excluded. Used the exact original 1896 public-domain Pawnee view in the Library of Congress scan.
